name: Watertown
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Watertown, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Watertown, MA: the Merry Mingle tree lighting at the Commander's Mansion with a parade, Santa photos, storytime and crafts.
lede: Watertown gathers at the historic Commander's Mansion for the Merry Mingle, the city's official tree lighting, with a parade, Santa photos and a toy drive.
celebrates: The City of Watertown celebrates the season with the Merry Mingle at the Commander's Mansion on Talcott Avenue. A parade walks from the Branch Line roundabout to the mansion lawn, and the winner of the city's coloring contest serves as Grand Marshal and lights the tree. Inside, the library reads holiday stories, the Recreation Department runs kids' games, and rooms show how families celebrate winter holidays around the world. Santa poses for photos, local dancers and school choirs perform, and a toy drive collects gifts for the Whooley Foundation. The Armenian Cultural and Educational Center on Nichols Avenue also holds a holiday celebration of its own.
lastyear: In 2025 the Merry Mingle took place on Saturday, December 6, from 4 to 8 pm at the Commander's Mansion. The city's announcement promised holiday characters, train rides, an artificial snowball fight with Watertown Recreation and a Christmas tree lighting at 7:30 pm. The WPS All City Chorus and Orchestra performed, kids made River of Light lanterns, and Santa photo sessions cost $10 each, with proceeds for future community events.
facts: The Commander's Mansion was built for Major Thomas J. Rodman, commander of the Watertown Arsenal, which opened in 1816 after President James Madison sent Captain George Talcott to find a site near Boston. Critics claimed the house would cost up to $150,000. The real cost was $63,478.65, close to $1 million in today's money. The mansion joined the National Register of Historic Places in 1976 and now hosts the city's tree lighting.
trains: Watertown has no MBTA Commuter Rail station of its own. The nearest stations are Waverley in Belmont and Waltham on the Fitchburg Line, and Newtonville on the Framingham/Worcester Line, all a short drive or bus ride away. For a real holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through its Christmas lights, and the Boston Street Railway Association shares the history of the area's streetcars and buses.

faq: Where is the Watertown tree lighting?

Watertown's official tree lighting, the Merry Mingle, happens at the Commander's Mansion, 440 Talcott Avenue. A parade leads families from the Branch Line roundabout to the mansion lawn, and the child who wins the city's coloring contest pulls the lever as Grand Marshal. The city lists the event as free admission, and it goes on rain or shine.
Where can I park for events at the Commander's Mansion?

For the Merry Mingle the city offers free parking in the East Garage behind 311 Arsenal Street, next to the Mosesian Center for the Arts, with accessible parking on Talcott Avenue at the mansion. From the garage it is a short walk to the Branch Line roundabout where the parade gathers.

It is the home built after the Civil War for Major Thomas J. Rodman, commanding officer of the Watertown Arsenal. The Italianate mansion has cast iron columns and patterned wood floors, cost $63,478.65 to build and has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1976. Today it hosts events, including the city's tree lighting.
How can my family donate toys in Watertown?

The Merry Mingle includes a toy drive for the Whooley Foundation. Families can bring a new toy to the tree lighting, and the Commander's Mansion also accepts toy donations on weekdays from Wednesday to Friday between 9 am and 2 pm during the drive, so you can drop off a gift even if you miss the evening.
